data.title: Table
data.tagline: Compare many records across the same columns
data.description: Tables suit orders, members, inventory, and other records that share the same fields. Sorting, filtering, and pagination each need deliberate behavior. When there are many columns, plan for smaller screens, horizontal scrolling, and clear header relationships.

use: Select several rows for a bulk action
avoid: Use a table for content that has no shared columns
Put every possible field on screen at once
Show too many columns unchanged on a narrow phone
Use a tree when the task is really comparing several fields

lessonPractice.title: Support staff need to compare the ID, amount, status, and date of 50 orders. Which presentation fits best?

options.label: Use one card per order and stack the four fields vertically
options.feedback: Cards help browse rich individual items, but vertically scattered fields make cross-order comparison slow.

options.label: Use one order per row and align the four fields in fixed columns
options.feedback: Every record shares the same fields, and fixed columns make amounts, statuses, and dates easy to compare.

options.label: Show one order at a time as a list of field names and values
options.feedback: A description list is useful for one record, but switching records removes the side-by-side comparison the task needs.

data.agentPrompt: Turn the order list into a table with one order per row and fixed ID, amount, status, and date columns while keeping current filters. Preserve essential columns on mobile and expose the rest by horizontal access or details. Verify rows remain aligned after sorting.
